text:
Carol will likely win, because the seller materially misrepresented the car: the ad and website pictured a 1964 model, but the car delivered was a 1968. An "as is" clause disclaims implied warranties, such as merchantability and fitness. It doesn't disclaim express warranties, and a description of the goods that is part of the basis of the bargain creates one (UCC 2-313). The "as is" clause therefore doesn't protect the seller. Of the choices, D comes closest, though A is the other plausible pick, since the picture issue is a distraction from the real problem, which is the wrong model year.

CONFIDENCE: 66
